claim:
Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\), where
\[
N(s,t)=\max\{|s|,|t|,|s-t|\}.
\]
Define
\[
IB'(X)=\inf\left\{\inf_{\lambda\in\mathbb R}N(x+\lambda y):x\in S_X,\ 0<N(y)\le1,\ N(x+y)=N(x-y)\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
IB'(X)=D(X)=\frac89,
\]
where \(D(X)\) is the same infimum with \(x,y\in S_X\). Every pair attaining \(IB'(X)\) has \(N(y)=1\), and, up to a linear isometry of \(X\) and replacement of \(y\) by \(-y\), the unique extremal pair is
\[
x=\left(1,\frac23\right),\qquad y=\left(\frac13,-\frac23\right).
\]
integrity: The proof exhausts relative edge positions, uses exact duality, and derives equality conditions symbolically. No numerical search is used as proof.
scientific_limitations: Specific to the real affine-regular Day--James endpoint. The scalar 8/9 has indirect later coverage; the new content is the bounded-domain lower bound and equality classification.
title: Unique extremal orbit for the bounded Birkhoff--isosceles discrepancy of the Day--James hexagon
